otx_pulses.title: False Protection, Emptied Accounts: The Seven Android Trojan Families Targeting Indian Banking Apps
otx_pulses.description: Group-IB's Threat Intelligence team uncovered a sophisticated Android malware campaign systematically targeting India's financial services sector since July 2025, orchestrated by the financially-motivated threat cluster CyberDakait. The operation distributes seven distinct malware families through coordinated smishing and vishing campaigns, impersonating bank representatives to trick victims into installing malicious APKs. These trojans harvest sensitive banking credentials, credit card details, and outstanding balances through overlay attacks while simultaneously conducting cryptojacking using XMRig. The malicious applications are hosted on GitHub repositories to maintain legitimacy, with the initial APK functioning as a dropper for the main payload and cryptocurrency mining module. Analysis revealed at least 17,960 compromised devices with 7.6 million intercepted SMS messages, including OTPs and transaction notifications. Attackers primarily target victims through fraudulent Credit Card Protection Plan s...

otx_pulses.title: Inside "MR ROBOT" - Anatomy of a Malware-as-a-Service Operation Targeting Indian Bank Customers
otx_pulses.description: A sophisticated Android Malware-as-a-Service operation called MR ROBOT is actively targeting Indian bank customers through a subscription-based model. The platform enables cybercriminals to rent customized banking trojans distributed via fake Play Store pages and messaging apps. The operation uses a multi-stage dropper that decrypts encrypted payloads to deploy banking trojans capable of intercepting SMS and OTPs, silently enabling call forwarding using the *21# carrier code to bypass phone-based two-factor authentication, and overlaying phishing screens to harvest card details, CVV, ATM PINs, UPI credentials, and identity documents. One tracked affiliate compromised 153 devices and intercepted 5,407 SMS messages across multiple Indian banks. The operation features a Telegram bot storefront offering approximately 36 fake applications impersonating banks, utility providers, and government services, with stolen data exfiltrated to Firebase Realtime Database and Telegram channels.

otx_pulses.title: SkyW4lker Phishing Kit: Microsoft 365 Threat to US Firms
otx_pulses.description: SkyW4lker is an active device-code phishing kit exploiting Microsoft 365 authentication processes across the United States, Europe, and other regions. Operating since June 2026, it bypasses MFA by abusing legitimate OAuth 2.0 device-code flows, granting attackers access to corporate accounts without stealing passwords. The kit uses phishing emails with password-protected attachments containing links that lead victims through CAPTCHA pages to malicious sites requesting Microsoft device codes. Analysis revealed 618 sandbox submissions between June and October 2026, with 46% originating from US organizations. Monthly activity surged from 20 cases in June to 200 in September. Technical investigation uncovered shared infrastructure and code similarities with the Gabagool credential phishing kit, suggesting common development. The kit employs obfuscated JavaScript, IP-based geolocation, and PHP backends to track victim authentication status, primarily targeting technology, manufacturing, and government sectors.
tags: target:United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

otx_pulses.title: Domain Shadowing: Attackers Abuse Institutional Domains
otx_pulses.description: Two unrelated operations exploited domain shadowing techniques to place illegal gambling content beneath legitimate educational and government domains in Bangladesh, India, and Mexico. Unauthorized parties gained access to DNS administration, creating records beneath established institutional namespaces to leverage their reputation for search engine optimization. Hidden Hawk added individual CNAME records mapping institutional hostnames to gambling pages hosted primarily on Cloudflare Pages, affecting over 850 entry points across eight domains. A separate campaign targeting Maharashtra government domains delegated entire subzones to third-party nameservers using wildcards, enabling external management of numerous hostnames. Both operations served Indonesian and Indian illegal gambling content worth an estimated $6 trillion globally in unregulated markets, exploiting institutional trust to boost search rankings and acquire traffic while leaving primary websites intact and potentially unnoticed by domain own...

otx_pulses.title: Suspected DPRK Campaign staging PHP2Shell Targeting against Global PHP infrastructure
otx_pulses.description: A Korean-speaking threat actor, tracked as the June 2026 Minjun campaign and linked with moderate confidence to North Korea's Lazarus Group, is actively planning targeted exploitation of two critical PHP vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619) that enable unauthenticated remote code execution. The campaign prioritizes government agencies, financial institutions, manufacturing, logistics, aviation, and trading platforms across the US, Japan, Thailand, Indonesia, Korea, Australia, Taiwan, India, Singapore, UAE, Saudi Arabia, and the EU. Operators are using AI-assisted reconnaissance to rank public exploit code and plan sector-specific attacks. Exploitation attempts have been observed globally since 17 October 2026, with 17 suspected source IPs identified conducting web shell deployment and session poisoning. The vulnerabilities affect all internet-facing PHP installations below version 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, or 8.2.35, with Apache mod_php at highest risk.

otx_pulses.title: Inside a Global AI-Assisted Hacking Campaign
otx_pulses.description: In October 2026, a Chinese-speaking threat actor conducted widespread AI-assisted cyberattacks combining the ARTEX penetration testing framework with multiple AI coding assistants including Claude Code, Codex, and Grok. The attacks, initially reported as targeting South Korean financial institutions, affected organizations globally across multiple industries including finance, retail, education, cryptocurrency, and telecommunications. Custom synchronization scripts maintained investigation context across AI sessions, while specialized agents divided reconnaissance and exploitation tasks. Prompts revealed requests for bulk personal data, transaction records, and mobile phone numbers, alongside questions about selling stolen information on underground markets. The workflow incorporated peer review between AI models, with GLM instructed to audit DeepSeek findings. Targeting spanned over 20 countries across Asia, Africa, Europe, and North America, indicating financially-motivated opportunistic attacks.
tags: target:United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

otx_pulses.title: "Next Exploit Opportunities": How a Threat Actor Used AI to Help Plan and Execute Multiple Types of Cybercrime Activities
otx_pulses.description: A financially motivated threat actor operating under the handle BUGSTER leveraged jailbroken AI assistants, specifically the Hermes Agent framework with DeepSeek V4, to conduct multiple cybercrime operations across India. The actor, demonstrating limited technical skills but relying heavily on AI-generated scripts and reconnaissance, successfully exfiltrated over 5,200 personal records from a university database, conducted WordPress brute force attacks, and planned VoIP telecommunications fraud. Additional activities included Wi-Fi password cracking requiring physical proximity to targets, cryptocurrency whale reconnaissance, and development of credential scanning toolkits. The actor configured specialized AI bot profiles providing step-by-step criminal guidance, including fraud traffic ratios and carrier evasion techniques, demonstrating how AI lowers the skill barrier for cybercrime operations.

otx_pulses.title: Hirudo: From Fake Updates to Patched Banking Apps
otx_pulses.description: A new Android banking remote access trojan named Hirudo has been identified, combining credential theft with live remote control. It is delivered through shopping and entertainment apps that act as droppers, installing the trojan as a separate package behind fake update prompts. The malware replaces legitimate banking applications with patched versions that disable security checks from within the app itself. Eight Indonesian banking apps covering seven banks have been targeted with purpose-built replacements embedding a hooking engine. The campaign uses real advertising infrastructure including Amazon CloudFront for distribution, with targeting extending beyond Indonesia to China, India, Mexico, Morocco, Thailand, and Malaysia. Backend data from August 2026 revealed thousands of stolen credentials and device records.

otx_pulses.title: Open Season on Kapibala: Attacker Steals Over 18,000 Government Records Through WordPress Exploitation
otx_pulses.description: A suspected Chinese-speaking threat actor, operating from UTC+8 timezone and linked to Red Heron, conducted extensive exploitation campaigns from May through September 2026. The adversary maintained persistent use of a single IP address to target multiple technologies including WordPress, ZyXEL switches, and various enterprise platforms. In the most severe incident, the attacker exploited WordPress vulnerabilities CVE-2026-63030 and CVE-2026-60137 to breach a western government organization, stealing over 18,000 sensitive records containing credentials and personally identifiable information. Additionally, the actor exploited CVE-2026-7273 in ZyXEL GS1900 switches, compromising 996 devices across 48 countries and exfiltrating configurations and credentials. The attacker demonstrated sophisticated capabilities including custom tool development possibly leveraging large language models, privilege escalation attempts, and systematic data exfiltration using PowerShell-based collection and staging techniques.

otx_pulses.title: Don't Call Us, We'll Call Your APIs | TraderTraitor Backdoors Resurface on Victim With No Crypto Ties
otx_pulses.description: In 2026, the DPRK-sponsored Lazarus subgroup TraderTraitor continued campaigns targeting cryptocurrency entities, including a high-profile attack on LayerZero resulting in $292 million theft from KelpDAO. Following this disclosure, an additional victim was identified: a smaller IT services provider in India with no cryptocurrency connections. The compromise involved a DevOps engineer targeted through fake job interview lures containing weaponized Terraform coding projects. Malicious GitHub repositories used typosquatted provider domains to deliver macOS backdoors FLATROOF and ROOFDECK when victims executed terraform init. The backdoors enabled reconnaissance, credential theft, and cloud environment escalation. One day after LayerZero's public disclosure, attackers deployed an updated stripped version of ROOFDECK and removed earlier implants. Activity continued until June 2026, suggesting the threat actor ultimately abandoned the intrusion after determining insufficient value from the smaller target.
